items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: they had Ella Fitzgerald, she scat sings.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Why don't you tell me a little bit about that?

Well, it was during the second illness of John Bubbles, see. He was living up on Sugar Hill there at Park Fort Lincoln, on Edgecombe Avenue, and he sent us down to Connie's Carny's Inn and Chick Webb was playing there at the time and also a house band. And he hadn't discovered Ella Fitzgerald yet. And we were playing there and we was breaking in a new routine -- a new tap dance, and they used to have tap dancers' night down there on Fridays. They'd have a searching spot light -- a spot light would go searching…

projectionist -- the light man, electrician, and tell him who's sitting in the audience and where to stop the light. And whoever the light stopped on, they would have to get up and do one chorus of their version of a tap dance they was calling the Shim-Sham Shimmy. It was really from a chorus girl's encore dance. And that's what happened, see. Well, he eventually got -- he overcome -- he overcome the double pneumonia, you see, and -- but we were doing so good then until they decided that we should be an act all…
